newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economic growth slows in June quarter - NBNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ economic growth slows in June quarter - NBNZ.

text.p: New Zealand's economic growth slowed in the June quarter, National Bank of New Zealand Ltd said in a regional trends commentary on Friday.
The easing was relatively widespread, with the number of regions recording a slowdown in activity matching the number on the rise.
"The number of declining regions has not been this prevalent since early 1991, when activity in all but one of the 14 regions declined simultaneously," National Bank said.
More encouraging, however, was a 0.3 percent rise in New Zealand's economic activity in the latest quarter.
National Bank said that on a nation-wide basis, the key economic indicators that increased in June were: employment, real estate turnover, motor vehicle registrations and exports.
Declines were measured in business and consumer confidence, retail trade and commercial construction.
At 0.3 percent, economic growth in the North Island was slightly ahead of the South Island, which recorded growth of 0.2 percent.
"The nation-wide increase in economic activity rose to 2.6 percent in the 12 months to June, from 2.4 percent in the March year," National Bank said.
"The acceleration in growth was centred in the North Island, which rose from 2.6 percent in March to 2.9 percent in June."
In contrast, the South Island had experienced a slight easing in economic growth to 1.8 percent in June from 1.9 percent in March.

The South Island region of Otago recorded the largest rise in economic activity in the latest quarter, underpinned by a "spectacular" rise in commercial and residential building permits. Gisborne in the North Island recorded the biggest fall.
